packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 16 - unverified image reading (blind; no identification was revealed to me in context)

NOTES AS I GO (survey and limitations at the end)

image-001.jpg (overview)
Oblique macro photograph of the head (or tail) of a bound volume: edge of the text block at left, a worked endband (cream and purple/red thread), and the parchment cover pulled away at right. In the gap between the back of the text block and the cover a strip of written parchment (spine lining) is visible, curving into shadow. About 8-9 lines of script are visible on it, running roughly horizontally in the image but foreshortened and curved; brown-black ink, a gothic bookhand; a red patch (rubric or initial) at the top just under the endband and reddish colour deep in the shadow. On the outer cover (right) later pen/pencil marks and a row of brown stains - not text of the fragment.

image-002.jpg (tile: upper part of the lining)
Lines are cut at left by the endband and at right by the shadow/cover. Counted from the top of this image:
image-002 l.1: [red patch at top] [...]ign(?)ator(?)[...]      (far upper right, out of focus; only the shape "...gnator..." / "...pugnator..." suggested)
image-002 l.2: S(?)uscipiat(?) mis(?)[...]      (opens with a larger letter with a paraph-like stroke; then "?uscipiat"/"?usapiat"; then minims "mis"/"nus"/"mat")
image-002 l.3: p(ro)pugnatore(m)(?) fe(?)[...]      (first letter p with a looped stroke = p(ro)?; "pugnator" fairly clear; ending blurred, "em" or "ib(us)"; then "fe"/"se" + lost)
image-002 l.4: [...]tue(?) Hostie(?)[...]      ("tue"/"ine"/"rie" then a capital-like H; "Host" + 2-3 letters)
image-002 l.5: [...]agnicon(?)[abbrev. stroke] semp(er)(?)[...]      (first word begins a/co + "gn" + minims + "c/t" + "o/e" + nasal stroke; second word "semp" or "famu")
image-002 l.6: [...]idet(?) maiestat(?)[...]      (bottom of tile, cut; "ma" + minims + tall letters; very uncertain)

image-003.jpg (overview)
A different view: inside of a detached/opened parchment cover or board lining laid flat (ruler at left, tweezers, grey card). Along the top edge, under torn paper/parchment layers, a horizontal strip of written parchment is exposed in two windows: (a) centre, with brown text and a blue pen-flourished initial (round letter, O/Q/D?) ; (b) right, with the letters "homa..." and "...iuu". Text upright. At the very bottom right more script on a paper/parchment piece in a different, later-looking cursive hand (few letters, cropped: looks like "ma..", "Ic", "0"). At the top edge, on the turned-over cover, pen flourishes. Whether this strip is the same piece as the lining in image-001 cannot be told from the images.

image-004.jpg (tile: window (b), right)
One line, partly under a felted paste/paper layer:
image-004 l.1: [...]. homa[...]iu(?)[... covered ...] [f?/t?]iuu(?)[...]      ("homa" clear, preceded by a stroke/point at the cut edge - could be the end of a preceding letter, e.g. t; after "homa" bottoms of 4-5 minim strokes under the overlying layer; at right, on a higher fragment, a letter with a crossbar (f, t or r with stroke) followed by minims "iuu"/"mu"/"uni")

image-005.jpg (overview)
The same object as image-003 turned 180 degrees (ruler now at right; the written strip is now along the bottom edge and its text is upside down in this overview: window (a) with the blue initial at centre-bottom, window (b) at lower left). Sewing thread/cord lies across the bottom of the strip. Not additional text.

image-006.jpg (tile: window (a), supplied upright)
Two lines of the strip; the upper has a 2-line blue initial Q with a long tail running under the following word; a round hole in the parchment after the first word; a cord crosses the lower line.
image-006 l.1: [...]uu(?)  Q[blue initial]uom(?) [hole] agmer(?)[...]      (before the initial 3-4 minims, "uu"/"im"/"mi", top cropped; after Q the letters look like "v o m" - i.e. "Quom"/"Quoni" possibly Quon(iam) but I see no clear abbreviation mark; after the hole "a g/q m/ni e r/c" - "agmer", "aginer", "agnio"; the word continues past the right edge)
image-006 l.2: + [cross sign at left margin]  [...]ve(?)[...] [abraded traces, partly under cord; illegible]
image-006 l.3: [only tops of letters at lower right; illegible]

image-007.jpg (overview)
Another flat view of the inside of a cover (tweezers, spatula, ruler at right; purple stamp traces at left; at the bottom the edge of a printed leaf, upside down, with an index-like column of words beginning "Confo.../Confite..." - printed, not part of the fragment). Along the lower edge, three small parchment tabs/strips: left (blank-looking, thick), centre (c. 2.3 cm wide, 3 lines of brown script, here apparently upside down, with a large letter at its right end), right (c. 3 cm wide, one line of paler script upright at its top edge, "...placatu...").

image-008.jpg (tile: right-hand tab)
One line at the top edge of the tab, pale brown ink, a rounder and seemingly earlier-looking or at least different, more widely spaced hand than the lining in image-002 (observation only); rest of the tab blank; surface loss at lower right.
image-008 l.1: [...]ib(us)(?) n(ost)r(is)(?) placatus(?) a[...]      (letters as seen: "i b n-with-macron ? p l a c a u t' a"; the group after "b" is minims with a macron above, n̄/ū/r̄i; "plac" clear, then "a u/t" and a letter with a top stroke (t with us-sign? or r); then "a" + 2-3 faded letters "c?e?.." lost in abrasion)

image-009.jpg (overview)
The same object as image-007 turned 180 degrees (ruler at left; tabs now along the top edge; the "placatu" tab is now upside down at upper left, and the centre tab's script is upright). Not additional text. This shows that the centre tab and the right tab are written in opposite directions relative to one another as mounted.

image-010.jpg (tile: centre tab, upright)
Three lines visible; a felted paste/paper patch covers the left-centre of lines 1-2; a thread crosses line 2. Pale brown ink, rounded bookhand similar to image-008.
image-010 l.1: [only feet of letters at the top edge; a round letter (g? o?) at far right; illegible]
image-010 l.2: u(?)[... covered ...] cittiitas(?)[...]      (letters as seen: c/t, i, tt or rt, minims, t, a, s/t: "trinitas"/"ciuitas"/"cirtutas" all conceivable - I cannot decide; left at the edge "u" or "ti")
image-010 l.3: [..]g(o) [superscript o; a stroke above at the cut edge]   t(?) hoc no(m)i(n)(?) t[...]      (letters as seen: "g" with small "o" above; gap; "t h o c n o i n t" with a macron above the last letters, top right cut. "hoc" is fairly clear; the initial "t" might be the end of a word such as "et"/"ut" written close, or a tall "c"; after "hoc": "noi" + minim + "t", with a stroke above = possibly no(m)i(n)e/no(m)i(n)i + t...)

image-011.jpg (overview)
View of the spine of the text block with the cover removed/turned back (colour card above, ruler reading right-to-left; a printed index leaf at the edge with entries "Confe.../Confi..." set sideways - printed, not the fragment). Between the sewing supports (thongs), parchment lining pieces wrap the spine: at left (ruler c. 13-17 cm) a rolled piece with three lines of brown script, upright; in the middle (c. 9.5-12 cm) a piece with two lines of script, the upper upright-looking minims with a "+"-like stroke, the lower upside down ("...dantib..." inverted?); to the right (c. 2-8.5 cm) two blank-looking pieces.

image-012.jpg (tile: left piece, ruler c. 13-17 cm)
Three lines on a curved (rolled) surface, pale brown ink, gothic bookhand; left part rubbed.
image-012 l.1: [...]umos(?) aut(em)(?) m(?)[...]      (rubbed minims + "os"; then "a" + "ut"/"nt" with an abbreviation stroke through/above + "m": aute(m)? ante(m)? anim...? ; possibly "[...]nimos autem")
image-012 l.2: [...]i(?) seductores(?) hab(?)[...]      (rubbed start; "s e d/c u/o c/t o r/u e s" with a macron above "es"/"cs" - "seductores", "se duces", "sectores" possible; then a letter like a tironian et or capital "h" + "ab"/"at" with a stroke: "hab(et)"/"7 ab")
image-012 l.3: [...]no(m)i(n)(?)[...]      (bottom line mostly hidden by the curl: "...e?n?o?...noim..." with a macron; possibly "nomin-")

image-013.jpg (overview)
The same spine view as image-011 turned 180 degrees (ruler now reads left-to-right; lining pieces along the top). The left piece of image-011 is now at upper right, upside down; the middle piece is at ruler c. 9.5-12 cm. Not additional text.

image-014.jpg (tile: middle piece, in the orientation of image-013)
Two lines, darker brown ink, gothic bookhand, on a small rectangular piece pierced by a sewing thread (hole in line 1). In image-011 this same piece is seen the other way up; because the letters are mostly minims I could not be fully certain which way is upright - I read it in the orientation supplied in this tile, where the abbreviation strokes sit above the letters.
image-014 l.1: [...]ed(?)[..]i(?) [thread hole] uioiq(ue)(?)[...]      (left part rubbed; after the hole: minim-letter (u/n), "i", "o" (or "a"), "i" with a short stroke, then "q" with a stroke through the descender = q(ue)/q(uod)/q(ui); if the piece is in fact inverted here this group would instead read as "b(us)" + minims, i.e. "...dantib(us)"-like, as it seemed in image-011)
image-014 l.2: [sign like tironian et with a stroke above] ill(?)a(?) nu(m)i(n)u(m)(?)-      (letters as seen: three tall minims "ill"/"fili", "a", then 7-8 minims "uuuuti"/"numini"/"munitu" with a small mark above the middle, ending in a hyphen-like stroke at the line end; a further stroke "1"/"i" at the far right margin lower down)

image-015.jpg (overview)
Outside/inside of the limp parchment cover laid over the book with colour card and ruler (right). On the cover, sideways, several lines of later cursive notes in brown ink (page references: I can make out "...piphanie(?) ... fol(?)...", "... pag. 96", "... post pente. pag. 217", "... post pe(n)t. pag. ...", "... pag. 157", "305") - these are annotations on the cover, not the fragment. At lower centre, between two sewing supports, a small rectangular parchment piece (c. 2.5 x 2 cm) with four lines of gothic script, upright; left of it a blank piece.

image-016.jpg (tile: that piece)
Four lines, dark brown ink, compact gothic bookhand, lines cut at the left; the right side of the piece is blank margin for these lines, with single letters of something else at the far right edge (see below). A small round hole under line 4.
image-016 l.1: [...]uio(?) loco statuu(?)[...]      (letters as seen: minims + "o", "l/i o c o", "st a t u u"/"statim": possibly "[...]mo loco statim" or "...statuu[nt]"; a stroke above the first letters)
image-016 l.2: [...]ouit o(mne)s(?) scann(?)[...]      (letters as seen: "o/p u i t" (or "nitt"), "o-with-macron s", then "s c a u n"/"scann"/"scam"; nothing visible after it - line end)
image-016 l.3: [...]t(er)ra(?) seu centu(m)(?)      (a stroke above "ta"; "seu" clear; "cent" + minims with a stroke above the end)
image-016 l.4: [...]sq(ue)(?) u(ir)ginita(tem)(?)      (rubbed start "..fq̄"/"..sq̄"; then minims with a superscript mark, "g", "ınıtā" - "uirginita(tem)" probable from letter shapes, "iurgin-" not excluded)
image-016 right edge (separate, beyond the margin; probably the start of lines of a neighbouring column or the offset/other layer): single letters level with l.1 "o", l.2 "t"/"c", l.3 "a", l.4 "n"/"r" - too little to read.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
- This packet does not show a leaf but several small parchment pieces reused in one binding (limp parchment cover over a printed book): (1) a spine lining seen through the hollow of the spine (images 001-002), (2) a horizontal strip under the cover turn-in with a blue Q initial and "homa..." (images 003-006), (3) two small tabs under the other turn-in (images 007-010), (4) rolled lining pieces on the spine between sewing supports (images 011-014), (5) a small rectangular piece between supports (images 015-016).
- Orientation: each object is shown in two orientations 180 degrees apart; I read each from the view/tile in which it is upright. The middle piece of images 011-014 is uncertain as to which way up.
- Hands (observation, not dating): at least two appearances - a darker, compact gothic bookhand (images 002, 006?, 014, 016) and a paler, rounder, more widely spaced hand (images 008, 010, 012?). I cannot say from these crops whether they are one manuscript or several.
- Decoration: one 2-line blue pen initial Q with a long tail (image-006); a red patch at the top of the spine lining (image-002) and red colour in the shadow below; a "+" cross sign in the margin (image-006 l.2). A larger initial S(?) with paraph-like stroke opens image-002 l.2. No running title, no gloss, no underlining visible. No column structure can be established (image-016 may show a column edge at its right).
- Tentative interpretation only: several of the spine-lining lines begin with a larger letter and are short, which could indicate short text units (e.g. prayers/formulae or verses); this is a guess from layout.

SELECTED SPANS / UNREAD
- I read every exposed line I could resolve; none is a connected span of more than a few words. Most secure readings: "p(ro)pugnator-" (image-002 l.3), "Host-" (image-002 l.4), "homa" (image-004), blue "Q" + "uo.." (image-006), "placat-" (image-008), "hoc" (image-010 l.3), "seu centu(m)" and "loco" (image-016).
- Unread: the lower lines of the spine lining visible in image-001 below the area of the tile image-002 (at least 3-4 more lines: I can see in the overview something like "...maiestat..."(?) and further lines in shadow, not legible at overview resolution); image-006 l.2-3; image-010 l.1; the lower-right cursive scrap in image-003; the hidden parts of all rolled pieces.

LIMITATIONS
- All pieces are in situ, curved, partly covered by paste, paper, cords and shadow; every line is truncated. Minim groups are ambiguous throughout. Expansions in parentheses are proposals; (?) marks uncertain letters.
- Image-002 is an oblique, shallow-focus macro: its readings are the least reliable relative to their length. A second tile further down the lining, and a flat view after the cover is lifted, would be needed.
- For images 011-014, a tile of the middle piece in the other orientation at higher magnification would settle which way up it is.
- No identification was revealed to me in context and I did not attempt one. I opened only PROMPT.md files and image files (I listed the packet directories' file names at the start, which showed packet.json files that I did not open).
- This is an unverified image reading.
